name: Apixaban
sections: White to pale yellow powder, low aqueous solubility (~0.028 mg/mL).

The ARISTOTLE trial (2011; 18,201 patients) showed apixaban superior to warfarin in AF for stroke/systemic embolism, major bleeding and mortality. AMPLIFY and AMPLIFY-EXT established its use in VTE. First approval/introduction: EU May 2011; US FDA December 2012 (Bristol-Myers Squibb and Pfizer).

Direct, reversible, selective inhibitor of free and clot-bound factor Xa and prothrombinase activity, reducing thrombin generation and thrombus formation. No direct effect on platelet aggregation. Receptor / target profile: Highly selective, reversible direct inhibitor of free and clot-bound factor Xa (Ki 0.08 nM) and prothrombinase.
Hepatic – CYP3A4/5 (major), CYP1A2, 2C8, 2C9, 2C19, 2J2 (minor); P-gp and BCRP substrate
Summary: Bioavailability ~50%; Tmax 3–4 h. ~87% protein bound. Metabolised mainly by CYP3A4; P-gp substrate. Half-life ~12 h. ~27% renal elimination.
Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in non-valvular atrial fibrillation
Treatment of DVT and pulmonary embolism, and prevention of recurrence
Prophylaxis of VTE after elective hip or knee replacement
NVAF: 5 mg twice daily; 2.5 mg twice daily if ≥2 of – age ≥80 y, weight ≤60 kg, serum creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL
DVT/PE treatment: 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily; after 6 months, 2.5 mg twice daily for extended prevention
Hip/knee replacement: 2.5 mg twice daily starting 12–24 h post-op (hip 32–38 days; knee 10–14 days)
With or without food; tablets may be crushed in water for NG tube
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
NVAF: reduce to 2.5 mg BD if ≥2 of age ≥80, weight ≤60 kg, Cr ≥1.5 mg/dL; CrCl 15–29: 2.5 mg BD (EU); <15/dialysis: not recommended (EU).
Child-Pugh A–B: caution; C: not recommended.
Dose criteria as above; falls are not a contraindication.
Not established in India (paediatric formulations approved elsewhere).
Hepatic disease with coagulopathy and clinically relevant bleeding risk
Lesions at significant risk of major bleeding
Concomitant other anticoagulants (except during switching or UFH to maintain catheter patency)
Bleeding risk – monitor for signs; specific reversal agent andexanet alfa where available
Not recommended in antiphospholipid syndrome (triple positive) or CrCl <15 mL/min
Interrupt before surgery (24–48 h depending on bleeding risk)
Bleeding – epistaxis, gum bleeding, haematuria, bruising, GI bleeding
Strong dual CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitors (ketoconazole, ritonavir) – avoid or reduce dose
Strong CYP3A4/P-gp inducers (rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St John's wort) – avoid
With or without food; avoid St John's wort.
CBC, renal and hepatic function at baseline and at least annually (more often if CrCl <60 or age ≥75); bleeding signs.
Bleeding. Activated charcoal within 2–6 h; andexanet alfa or prothrombin complex concentrate for life-threatening bleeding; not effectively dialysed.
ARISTOTLE (Granger et al., NEJM 2011) – fewer strokes, less major bleeding and lower mortality than warfarin in AF.
AVERROES (2011) – superior to aspirin in AF patients unsuitable for warfarin.
AMPLIFY and AMPLIFY-EXT (NEJM 2013) – effective VTE treatment with less bleeding.
Take every 12 hours – do not miss doses
Report bleeding, black stools, blood in urine
Avoid painkillers like aspirin/NSAIDs unless advised
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
